newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-RUSSIANS STRIKE GOLD ON OPENING DAY.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-RUSSIANS STRIKE GOLD ON OPENING DAY.

text.p: Yelena Vialbe did it again and Alexei Prokurorov made it at last as Russia stole the show on the opening day of the Nordic skiing world championships on Friday.

Vialbe's victory in the 15 km freestyle ahead of Stefania Belmondo of Italy and Katerina Neumonnavo was no great surprise as the most successful woman in cross-country skiing history had already collected nine world titles.

But Prokurorov's triumph in the 30 km freestyle was totally unexpected -- and also a big disappointment for Norway, who had to be happy with the silver for Bjorn Daehlie and the bronze for Thomas Alsgaard.
Few would have bet on the 32-year-old Prokurorov, who had not won gold in any of his previous five world championships and had not finished in the top 10 in World Cup meetings this season.
"I didn't expect to do so well," said Prokurorov after covering two laps of a bumpy 15-km circuit in a winning time of one hour six minutes 28 seconds.
Most of the thousands of fans lining the track on a beautiful day were hoping for another win by Daehlie, the male counterpart of Vialbe with six world titles already.
Daehlie made the strongest start but after 15 kms was two seconds slower than Prokurorov and had to settle for second place 17 seconds behind.
Young Alsgaard, who was feeling sick and decided to enter the race only at the last minute, brought some consolation for Norway by taking third place, 21 seconds behind Prokurorov.
The race was a nightmare for world champion Vladimir Smirnov of Kazakhstan, who struggled from the start end ended a poor 42nd.
Daehlie, seeming almost effortless as he climbed a steep hill nearly halfway through the course, clocked the fastest intermediate time after seven kilometres.

"I didn't hear about Prokurorov until the end of the first lap when I learned he was two seconds ahead of me," said the Norwegian. "I was a little bit surprised but I understood it would be a tough battle between him and me for the gold medal."
Daehlie then failed to keep up with the pace set by Prokurorov, losing ground on the Russian in the second lap.
"Conditions were absolutely perfect and the atmosphere was fantastic with all those people waving Norwegian flags," said Daehlie.
"It was like a dream and at one stage, I thought I could go for gold but a silver medal is fine. There are more races to come and I didn't expect to be in such great shape."
Prokurorov, whose best result this season was an 11th place last December in Oberstdorf, Germany, said he was also surprised at his form.
"I haven't been feeling that well lately but today everything was just perfect," said the Russian, adding he would carry on until next year's winter Olympics in Nagano, Japan.

The weather changed dramatically after the men's race and it was cloudy when Vialbe set off. Snow began to fall but that did not stop her from being fastest at all intermediate times before winning in 36 minutes 28 seconds.
The 28-year-old Vialbe, who will, like Prokurorov, end her career in Nagano, was 11 seconds faster than Belmondo while Neumannova finished a further three seconds back.
"It's like the first time," she said. "I never get tired of winning."
Belmondo, who had promised to look for gold in every race in the 10-day meeting, said there was very little she could do.
"Yelena was just too strong today but I'll keep trying," she said.
